clips.caption: The speaker welcomes the audience and introduces Michael Daigler as a key figure in his journey into hackathons and event hosting.
The speaker shares how meeting Michael Daigler at a meta hackathon led to mentorship and connections with the AITX community.
Michael Daigler discusses his shift from relying on MCP to using Appify Actors for reliable, repeatable web data workflows.
The speaker identifies challenges in using native web tools for scraping data from sites like LinkedIn and Reddit, and the lack of consistency in results.
He introduces the concept of creating reusable 'tools' like a hammer—pre-built, reliable, and efficient for repeated tasks.
The speaker explains how he applies the workflow and worker paradigm to structure repeatable, auditable, and consistent data workflows.
He highlights Appify as a platform that provides reliable web scraping tools with anti-bot bypass capabilities for real-time data access.
A detailed example of a workflow to find ideal sponsorship contacts on LinkedIn using AI-driven search, fuzzy matching, and profile scraping.
The speaker frames his approach as building a personal 'toolbox'—a centralized library of reusable tools for AI agents.
He demonstrates the workflow in action using Cloud Code, showing how to initiate a search and scrape LinkedIn profiles for sponsorship leads.
The speaker introduces a workflow using AI actors to automate tasks like finding relevant contacts on LinkedIn for event sponsorships.
The speaker demonstrates how a custom skill scrapes LinkedIn data to identify key personnel for hackathon sponsorships.
The speaker explains the separation between the skill (in Claude) and the actor (cloud-based), emphasizing lightweight, modular design.
The speaker highlights the importance of abstracting business logic into reusable tools to streamline agent-driven workflows.
The speaker identifies and validates a high-potential contact at Google Cloud, emphasizing relevance and background for outreach.
The speaker suggests tailoring outreach messages by aligning with the target’s professional identity and emotional motivations.
The speaker presents AgentMail.2 as an API-first email tool for automating outreach with tested, high-performing templates.
The speaker shares a $100 credit for Appify platform usage, restricted to Appify-maintained actors to support community creators.
The speaker clarifies that only publicly accessible data is scraped, and private accounts are excluded, with proxy systems ensuring human-like behavior.
The speaker concludes with a self-paced workshop plan, inviting participants to replicate the workflow and offering support during checkpoints.
The speaker begins the workshop by outlining the structure and goals of the session.
The speaker encourages participants to get ready, sets up background music, and energizes the audience.
The speaker explains the purpose of the workshop, emphasizing the importance of reading the readme for setup.
The speaker starts cloning the repository and setting up the project environment.
The speaker introduces the main idea: building custom tools for AI agents using local workflows.
The speaker discusses the need for an Anthropic API key and alternatives like Gemini.
The speaker explains creating a modular toolbox for organizing reusable workflows.
The speaker walks through a real example of scraping LinkedIn profiles and analyzing data.
The speaker shares insights on effective outreach, prioritizing experienced professionals.
The speaker concludes by summarizing the workflow, sharing code, and discussing API key handling.
The speaker begins by introducing the workflow and setting up the environment, emphasizing the importance of dependencies and inputs like company URL and prompt.
The speaker outlines the main workflow structure, explaining the entry point and the three key inputs required for the process.
The speaker discusses the time constraints and audience familiarity, clarifying that the session is meant as a demonstration rather than a hands-on build.
The speaker explains the first worker, 'make search query,' which generates job titles based on intent from the initial question.
The speaker details how employee data is scraped from LinkedIn and passed to the profile worker for further processing.
The speaker suggests automating the workflow by running it repeatedly until desired output standards are met.
The speaker guides through setting API keys, running the workflow, and moving it to a global directory for accessibility.
The speaker explains how to generate a skill for the agent using the workflow, ensuring it knows where to run the process.
The speaker wraps up with key actions: setting tokens, running the workflow, and mentions useful tools like 'understand anything' and 'Git ingest'.
The speaker concludes by encouraging practical use of Appify in daily work and thanks the audience for their attention.
